newsitem.title: USA: Clinton condemns IRA killing of two policemen.
newsitem.headline: Clinton condemns IRA killing of two policemen.

text.p: President Bill Clinton on Monday condemned the killing of two Northern Ireland policemen by Irish Republican Army (IRA) guerrillas, saying that he was outraged by the "cowardly killings."

"I am outraged by the callous murder by the IRA of two policemen in Northern Ireland," Clinton said in a written statement released by the White House. "I condemn this brutal act of terrorism in the strongest possible terms."
IRA guerrillas killed the policemen in an ambush in the town of Lurgan, throwing the halting Northern Ireland peace process into turmoil.

"There is nothing patriotic or heroic about these cowardly killings," Clinton said, warning against retaliation. "Further violence can only play into the hands of those responsible for the vicious murders of the two policemen."
Clinton also pledged to keep working for peace.

"I will continue to do all I can to suport ... the efforts of the political leaders participating in the Belfast peace talks," he said, referring to multi-party talks under the chairmanship of former U.S. Senator George Mitchell.
The talks, which resumed this month after a three-month hiatus, have been bogged down for a year because of basic distrust between majority Protestants and minority Catholics.

White House spokesman Mike McCurry earlier condemned the shootings and called called on pro-British Loyalist guerrillas, who have maintained a shaky truce since October 1994, not to retaliate for the policemen's killings.
Asked if the United States expected to continue to have contacts with Sinn Fein, the White House spokesman hinted at growing U.S. frustration with the political wing of the IRA.
"We will continue the contacts that we believe are helpful to the process, but sooner or later it becomes clear who is willing to help the process and who is not," McCurry said.
The IRA shattered its 18-month-long ceasefire with a bombing in London in February 1996.
